name: Roil
author: E. T. Carter
description: A turbulent current of dense fine fibres advected through a churning field — curl-noise plus a handful of slowly orbiting vortices wind the threads into spiralling eddies that wind up, shear apart and reform. Colour follows the local flow direction so opposing swirls glow in different palette hues, with two parallaxing depth layers churning at different rates. The chaotic cousin of the combed warp-current.

params.label: Thread count
params.effect: Density of fibres in the current; low gives a few broad streaks, high a fine churning weave.

params.label: Churn
params.effect: Strength of the curl-noise turbulence bending the fibres; 0 leaves a near-straight flow, high boils it into dense chaos.

params.label: Vortices
params.effect: Pull of the orbiting point vortices; 0 removes the big whorls, high winds the fibres into tight spiralling eddies.

params.label: Flow speed
params.effect: Master speed of the churning current; 0 holds a frozen turbulent still, high keeps the eddies restlessly reforming.

params.label: Glow
params.effect: Overall emission of the fibres; low is a dim undertow, high a luminous churning flood.

params.label: Hue spread
params.effect: How far the palette ranges with flow direction; 0 washes the whole current one hue, high cycles many colours as the eddies turn.

params.label: Depth
params.effect: Parallax separation between the near and far fibre layers and how much the far one dims; low flattens them, high sinks the far churn back into shadow.

params.label: Mouse influence
params.effect: How strongly the pointer stirs the current; the cursor winds a local vortex and drags the fibres toward it, easing back with distance. 0 ignores the mouse.

params.label: Mouse radius
params.effect: Reach of the pointer stir in frame units; small is a fingertip eddy, large drags a wide swathe of the current.
